title: AI crawler signature catalog
description: The signature list the middleware matches traffic against. Edit this file, host it, or point `catalog.source` at your own copy.

version.description: Shown in the dashboard and in generated robots.txt, so you can tell which list a site is running.

notes.description: Free-text notes for whoever maintains the file. Ignored by the engine.

id.description: Stable slug. Policy rules and stored events reference it, so renaming one orphans its history.

purpose.description: Groups the crawler in the dashboard and tells the owner what blocking it would cost them.

robotsToken.description: The token written to robots.txt. Must be unique case-insensitively across the file.

robotsOnly.description: True for opt-out controls that only exist in robots.txt and never appear in a User-Agent header (Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended). Such entries must not declare userAgentPatterns.

items.description: A case-insensitive substring, or `re:<pattern>` for a regular expression. The longest matching pattern wins across the whole catalog.

defaultAction.description: What this crawler gets when the site owner has expressed no opinion. Use sparingly - it overrides the site's own default.

note.description: Shown to the site owner beside the toggle.

methods.description: Tried in order. An empty array means the operator publishes no way to verify this crawler; do not invent one, because a wrong suffix blocks real crawlers.

hostnameSuffixes.description: Required by the `dns` method. Matched at a label boundary, so ".openai.com" never matches "notopenai.com".

ranges.description: Static CIDR prefixes, always checked by the `cidr` method.

rangesUrl.description: An operator-published prefix list. Only fetched when the middleware runs with verification.fetchRanges = true.
